top_buys.pitch: Repeated missile and drone strikes on Saudi airports make Gulf air-defense restocking a multi-quarter story.
top_buys.why: Houthi attacks hit Riyadh's airports twice in two days, killing civilians and forcing airlines to cancel flights, with the FAA warning US carriers. Saudi Arabia and Gulf partners are heavy buyers of US interceptors and radars, and defense budgets respond with a lag that the market usually under-prices. Lockheed makes the PAC-3 and THAAD systems at the center of that demand.
top_buys.risks: Saudi-Iranian foreign ministers are already talking, and any de-escalation would deflate the defense bid; defense stocks also move slowly without a concrete contract.
top_buys.watch: Any announced Gulf interceptor orders and Lockheed's Q3 earnings later this month.

top_buys.pitch: European storage at lows plus Middle East LNG hostage to the Iran war keeps US export economics tight.
top_buys.why: Reuters reports Europe is set for another year of high gas prices with reserves at multi-year lows, while Qatari and regional LNG flows remain at risk from the Hormuz standoff. Cheniere is the largest US exporter and benefits from sustained international gas price spreads. This is a slow-burn supply story rather than a one-day headline pop.
top_buys.risks: A Hormuz reopening deal or mild winter would crush European gas prices, and emerging Asian LNG demand is reportedly softening as renewables grow.
top_buys.watch: Iran's formal reply on the Hormuz proposal and European storage levels heading into winter.

top_buys.pitch: A $2.1B bolt-on in surgical products adds growth to a steady medtech compounder in a strong health care tape.
top_buys.why: STERIS agreed to buy Xodus Medical for $2.1B, expanding its operating-room consumables franchise where it already has scale and distribution. Acquirers in medtech typically see the accretion case build over weeks rather than being priced on day one. Health care was one of last week's best sectors, so the tide is favorable.
top_buys.risks: Investors may balk at the price or the added leverage, and integration risk is real for a deal this size.
top_buys.watch: Management's commentary on accretion and financing at the next earnings call.

top_buys.pitch: Bank earnings kick off Tuesday into a deal-making wave that favors the biggest advisory franchise.
top_buys.why: Goldman reports alongside JPMorgan, Citi and Wells this week, and the headlines are full of M&A: Salesforce buying Loops, STERIS buying Xodus, Amazon in talks for Decart, Solventum selling a unit. That advisory and capital-markets activity flows straight to Goldman's revenue line. Financials have also been a firm sector over the past week.
top_buys.risks: Dimon's warning about a corporate credit squeeze could sour the whole group, and bank stocks often sell off on good numbers after a run.
top_buys.watch: Goldman's Q3 results and investment-banking backlog commentary Tuesday morning.

top_buys.pitch: Microsoft's million-unit Maia 300 plan squeezes the merchant GPU challenger more than the leader.
top_buys.why: Microsoft unveiled its Maia 300 in-house AI chip with claims of 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems and plans to scale to a million units next year. Custom hyperscaler silicon mostly eats into the second-source GPU budget, which is where AMD hopes to grow. Tech was the weakest sector last week and AI hardware names sold off sharply Monday.
top_buys.risks: AI compute demand is big enough that both can win, and any large AMD customer announcement would reverse this quickly.
top_buys.watch: AMD's Q3 earnings and any new hyperscaler commitments for MI-series accelerators.
